From 1980 hundreds of thousands of Salvadorans fled the civil war and poverty, most to the United States. Today well over two million people of Salvadoran origin live there.

Many crossed Mexico without papers and settled in Los Angeles, Washington and Houston. The United States at first refused most of them asylum, as it was backing the government they fled. Later, after earthquakes in El Salvador in 2001, many were given temporary legal status.

Money sent home now makes up over a fifth of El Salvador's economy, and the country adopted the US dollar in 2001. The diaspora also brought back street gangs formed in Los Angeles. Like the later caravans, it is part of a vast movement from Central America to the north that began with the civil war.
sum: From 1980 hundreds of thousands of Salvadorans fled the civil war and poverty, most to the United States. Today well over two million people of Salvadoran origin live there.
